title: An HTTP server
summary: Build a web server with http.createServer that answers by path with status codes and JSON.

docs.title: Node.js: Anatomy of an HTTP transaction

quiz.q: In http.createServer((req, res) => { ... }), what is req?
options: An object describing the incoming request, such as its url and method
quiz.explain: `req` describes what the browser asked for (`req.method`, `req.url`, `req.headers`). You build the answer with `res`.

quiz.q: Complete the handler so it answers with status 200 and the text Hello.
quiz.explain: `res.writeHead(status, headers)` sets the status line and headers. `res.end(body)` sends the body and finishes the response. Forgetting `end` leaves the browser waiting forever.

quiz.q: Which status code means the page or resource was not found?
quiz.explain: `404 Not Found`. A `200` means success, `301` is a redirect and `500` means the server itself failed.

quiz.q: This server should send JSON. Which line is wrong?
quiz.explain: `res.end` needs a string or a Buffer, not an object. Convert it first: `res.end(JSON.stringify({ status: 'ok' }))`.

exercise.task:
In `server.js`, finish the server created with `http.createServer`. Answer these requests:

- `GET /` replies with status `200` and the text `Welcome`.
- `GET /health` replies with status `200`, the header `Content-Type: application/json` and the JSON body `{"status":"ok"}`.
- Any other path replies with status `404` and the text `Not Found`.

Do not call `server.listen`. The file ends with `module.exports = server;` so the checker can start it for you.
hints: Look at `req.url` inside the handler and use `if` statements to decide what to send.
For each answer call `res.writeHead(status, headers)` and then `res.end(body)`. For JSON the body must be a string: use `JSON.stringify`.
